questions.question: Who was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2025 for his contributions to Indian hockey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PR Sreejesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India** announced the **Padma Awards 2025** on the eve of the **76th Republic Day**, where legendary hockey goalkeeper **PR Sreejesh** was conferred with the **Padma Bhushan**.
 
• The **Padma Bhushan** is the **third-highest civilian award** in India, recognized for "distinguished service of a high order." **PR Sreejesh** received this honor for his monumental contributions to **Indian hockey** over a career spanning nearly two decades.
 
• Hailing from **Kizhakambalam, Kerala**, **PR Sreejesh** is widely regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers in the history of the sport, earning the nickname **"The Great Wall of Indian Hockey."**
 
• His career reached a historic peak when he played a crucial role in helping the **Indian Men’s Hockey Team** secure back-to-back **Olympic Bronze Medals** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• Following the **Paris 2024** campaign, where his stellar saves in the quarter-final against Great Britain and the bronze medal match against Germany were decisive, **Sreejesh** announced his **retirement** from international hockey in **August 2024**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Career and Achievements:**
 
 
• **PR Sreejesh** made his international debut for the senior national team in **2006** at the **South Asian Games** in Colombo.
 
• He served as the **Captain** of the Indian national team, leading them to a silver medal at the **2016 Champions Trophy** and a historic quarter-final appearance at the **2016 Rio Olympics**.
 
• He was awarded the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **2021**, India's highest sporting honor, and previously received the **Padma Shri** in **2017**.
 
• In **2021**, he became only the second Indian athlete to win the **World Games Athlete of the Year** award, following Rani Rampal.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Harvinder Singh:** A legendary **Para-archer** who made history by winning India's first-ever **Gold Medal** in archery at the **Paris 2024 Paralympic Games**. He was also considered for major honors in **2025**.
 
• **IM Vijayan:** A former **Indian Football** captain and three-time **AIFF Player of the Year**. Known as the "Black Pearl" of Indian football, he is a recipient of the **Arjuna Award**.
 
• **Satyapal Singh:** A renowned **Para-athletics coach** who has been instrumental in training several Indian medalists. He was awarded the **Dronacharya Award** for his coaching excellence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Padma Awards Structure:** The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (distinguished service of high order), and **Padma Shri** (distinguished service).
 
• **Selection Process:** The **Padma Awards Committee**, constituted by the **Prime Minister** every year, makes the recommendations, which are then approved by the **President of India**.
 
• **Legacy:** At the time of his retirement in **2024**, **PR Sreejesh** had earned over **330 international caps** for India. Post-retirement, he was appointed as the head coach of the **India U-21 Men's Hockey Team** to nurture future talent.
 
• **2025 Statistics:** The **2025 Padma list** highlighted a significant focus on sports icons who brought glory to the nation during the **Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic cycle**, emphasizing India's growing stature in global sports.

questions.question: Which of the following features is a major design focus for the Zorawar tank?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amphibious capability and lightweight design**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Zorawar** is an indigenous **Light Tank** developed primarily for the **Indian Army** to operate in difficult terrains where heavy main battle tanks face mobility issues.
 
• A major design focus for the **Zorawar** tank is its **lightweight design**, typically weighing around **25 tonnes**. This allow the tank to be easily transported by air via **C-17 Globemaster** aircraft and deployed rapidly in **high-altitude areas**. ***Hence, the statement regarding lightweight design is correct.***
 
• The tank is equipped with **amphibious capability**, which enables it to navigate across water bodies like rivers and lakes, a critical feature for operations in the **Himalayan region** and riverine terrains. ***Hence, the statement regarding amphibious capability is correct.***
 
• It has been developed collaboratively by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and **Larsen & Toubro (L&T)** to provide the **Indian Army** with a tactical advantage in the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**.
 
• The **Zorawar** tank is designed to feature high **mobility** and **firepower**, making it suitable for **mountain warfare** where traditional tanks like the **T-90** or **T-72** might struggle due to their weight exceeding **40-50 tonnes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Strategic Necessity:** The project was fast-tracked following the **2020 standoff** with **China** in **Eastern Ladakh**. The **People's Liberation Army (PLA)** had deployed its **Type 15 (ZTQ-15)** light tanks, prompting **India** to develop a similar indigenous capability.
 
• **Naming:** The tank is named after **General Zorawar Singh**, the legendary 19th-century military commander who led successful campaigns in **Ladakh**, **Baltistan**, and **Tibet**.
 
• **Technological Features:** It is expected to integrate **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)** integration for better situational awareness, and **Active Protection Systems (APS)** to defend against anti-tank guided missiles.
 
• **Power-to-Weight Ratio:** One of its defining features is a high **power-to-weight ratio**, ensuring it can climb steep gradients and navigate narrow passes in **high-altitude** regions exceeding **15,000 feet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Zorawar:** The **Indian Army** has expressed a requirement for approximately **354** of these light tanks to equip its armored regiments in **mountainous** sectors.
 
• **Trials:** The prototype of the **Zorawar** tank commenced internal trials in **July 2024**, with further **user trials** by the **Army** expected to follow in desert and **high-altitude** environments to test its performance under extreme temperatures.
 
• **Stealth and Detection:** While it incorporates modern electronic warfare suites, it is **not** designed for **naval stealth** or **submarine detection**, as those are naval technologies unrelated to armored land warfare.
 
• **Weaponry:** It is typically armed with a **105mm** main gun capable of firing various types of ammunition and **anti-tank missiles**, providing a balance between lethality and the constraints of a lighter chassis.
</ul

questions.question: In March 2025, Operation Brahma was launched by the NDRF to rescue earthquake victims of which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was officially launched in **March 2025** by the **Government of India** to provide urgent humanitarian assistance to **Myanmar** following a severe **earthquake**.
 
• The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** was the primary agency responsible for executing the search and rescue operations on the ground, deploying multiple specialized battalions. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The operation involved the deployment of **Indian Air Force (IAF)** transport aircraft, such as the **C-17 Globemaster III**, to ferry **NDRF** personnel, canine squads, and heavy rescue equipment to **Myanmar**.
 
• This mission was a critical part of India’s **“Neighborhood First” policy**, emphasizing rapid response to natural calamities in adjacent nations. ***Hence, statements 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect in the context of Operation Brahma.***
 
• The **NDRF** teams focused on extricating victims from collapsed structures and providing immediate medical aid through field hospitals set up in the affected zones of **Myanmar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**:
 
 
• The **NDRF** was constituted under Section 44 of the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and is a specialized force meant for responding to natural and man-made disasters.
 
• The **Director General (DG)** of **NDRF** is an **IPS officer** of the rank of Director General of Police.
 
 
 
• **India’s HADR Tradition**:
 
 
• **HADR** stands for **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief**. India has emerged as a **Net Security Provider** and first responder in the **Indian Ocean Region**.
 
• Previous notable operations include **Operation Dost** for **Turkey** and **Syria** in **2023**, and **Operation Maitri** for **Nepal** in **2015**.
 
 
 
• **India-Myanmar Relations**:
 
 
• India and **Myanmar** share a land border of approximately **1,643 km** and a maritime boundary in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• Cooperation in disaster management is a key pillar of the **Act East Policy** and **BIMSTEC** (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) framework.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Disaster Management Act** was enacted on **23rd December 2005**, which led to the creation of the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Operation Brahma** involved the distribution of relief materials including **medicines**, **blankets**, **tents**, and **ready-to-eat meals** to thousands of displaced persons in **Myanmar**.
 
• In **2025**, the use of advanced technology like **drones** and **ground-penetrating radars** by the **NDRF** significantly improved the efficiency of life-saving efforts during the operation.
</ul

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2022, seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, with respect to its application to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2022**, was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **December 9, 2022**, by the **Union Minister of Tribal Affairs**, **Shri Arjun Munda**.
 
• The primary objective of this bill is to amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**, specifically focusing on its application to the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• The bill seeks to include the **'Betta-Kuruba'** community as a synonym for the **'Kadu Kuruba'** community at **serial number 16** of the **Scheduled Tribes** list for **Karnataka**.
 
• This change was proposed because the **Betta-Kuruba** community had been facing difficulties in obtaining **Scheduled Tribe certificates** due to the absence of their specific name in the existing list, despite being ethnically identical to the **Kadu Kuruba**.
 
• The inclusion follows the formal recommendation of the **Government of Karnataka** and subsequent clearance by the **Registrar General of India (RGI)** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Framework for Scheduled Tribes**:
 
 
• Under **Article 342** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President**, after consultation with the **Governor** of a state, notifies the list of **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• Once the initial list is notified via the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**, any subsequent inclusion, exclusion, or modification can only be done through an **Act of Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Inclusion**:
 
 
• Members of the **Betta-Kuruba** community will now be eligible for benefits under various government schemes, such as **Post-Matric Scholarships**, **National Overseas Scholarships**, and **Top Class Education** for **ST** students.
 
• It also ensures **political representation** in **Reserved Constituencies** and **reservation** in government jobs under **Article 16(4)** of the **Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Process of Amendment**:
 
 
• The process begins with a proposal from the **State Government**, which is then sent to the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs**.
 
• The **Registrar General of India (RGI)** reviews the ethnographical details. If approved, it is sent to the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** for final consultation before being placed before the **Union Cabinet** and then **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Related 2022 Amendments**:
 
 
• Apart from **Karnataka**, the **Government of India** introduced similar bills in **2022** for states like **Tamil Nadu** (to include **Narikoravan** and **Kurivikkaran**), **Himachal Pradesh** (for **Hattee** community), and **Uttar Pradesh** (for **Gond** community in certain districts).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Betta-Kuruba** community traditionally resides in the hilly regions of **Kodagu**, **Mysuru**, and **Chamarajanagar** districts in **Karnataka**.
 
• They are traditionally known for their skills in **basket weaving** and **honey collection**.
 
• The term **'Betta'** means **Hill** and **'Kuruba'** refers to **Shepherd**, although this specific community is primarily forest-dwelling rather than pastoral.
 
• The **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2022** reflects the government's commitment to **'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas'** by providing social justice to marginalized communities.
</ul

questions.question: What is the theme of the 11th International Day of Yoga 2025?

options.text: Yoga for One Earth, One Health

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yoga for One Earth, One Health**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **11th International Day of Yoga (IDY)** is scheduled to be celebrated on **June 21, 2025**. The official theme designated for this year's celebration is **"Yoga for One Earth, One Health"**.
 
• This theme emphasizes the holistic nature of **Yoga** and its role in fostering a sustainable lifestyle that benefits not just individual human health, but the health of the entire **planet** and all its living beings.
 
• The **Ministry of Ayush** serves as the nodal agency in **India** for organizing the primary events and coordinating with various **international organizations** and **Indian missions** abroad to promote the practice of Yoga globally.
 
• The **2025 theme** aligns with the broader global vision of **One Health**, which recognizes that the health of **humans**, **animals**, and the **environment** are closely linked and interdependent.
 
• The **International Day of Yoga** aims to raise awareness about the **ancient Indian practice** of Yoga, which combines **physical postures (Asanas)**, **breathing techniques (Pranayama)**, and **meditation (Dhyana)** for overall well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin and Proposal:** The concept of an **International Day of Yoga** was first formally proposed by the **Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi**, during his speech at the **69th session** of the **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)** on **September 27, 2014**.
 
• **UN Resolution:** Following the proposal, the **UNGA** passed a resolution on **December 11, 2014**, declaring June 21 as the International Day of Yoga. Notably, the resolution was co-sponsored by a record **177 member states**.
 
• **Selection of June 21:** The date **June 21** was chosen because it marks the **Summer Solstice** in the **Northern Hemisphere**. It is the longest day of the year and holds historical and spiritual significance in many cultures, often associated with the transition toward **Dakshinayana** in the yogic tradition.
 
• **First Celebration (2015):** The inaugural **International Day of Yoga** was held on **June 21, 2015**. The main event took place at **Rajpath (now Kartavya Path)** in **New Delhi**, setting two **Guinness World Records** for the largest yoga session (**35,985 participants**) and for having the most nationalities (**84 countries**) represented in a single yoga event.
 
• **Previous Themes:** 
 
 
• The theme for the **10th edition (2024)** was **"Yoga for Self and Society"**.
 
• The theme for the **9th edition (2023)** was **"Yoga for Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam"**, which means "The World is One Family."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Common Yoga Protocol (CYP):** To standardize the celebration, the **Ministry of Ayush** developed the **Common Yoga Protocol**, which is a collection of simple yogic practices suitable for people of all ages and backgrounds.
 
• **Holistic Health:** Yoga is recognized by the **World Health Organization (WHO)** as a means to improve **physical health**, reduce **stress**, and manage **non-communicable diseases (NCDs)** such as hypertension and diabetes.
 
• **Global Participation:** Every year, millions of people participate in **IDY** events across iconic locations worldwide, including the **United Nations Headquarters** in **New York** and various **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**.
</ul

questions.question: What was India’s rank among the most polluted countries in the World Air Quality Report 2024, released in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **World Air Quality Report 2024**, which was released by the **Swiss organization IQAir** in **March 2025**, **India** was ranked as the **5th** most polluted country globally.
 
• The report evaluates air quality based on the concentration of **PM2.5** (particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers or less), which is considered the most harmful pollutant to human health.
 
• **India's** average annual **PM2.5** concentration was found to be significantly higher than the **World Health Organization (WHO)** annual air quality guideline of **5 µg/m³**.
 
• The **2024** report highlighted that a vast majority of the world's most polluted cities are located in **India**, particularly within the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** region.
 
• While **India** showed slight improvements in certain urban pockets compared to previous years, it remains a "high-pollution" zone due to industrial, vehicular, and construction activities. ***Hence, the correct answer is 5th.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding PM2.5:**
 
 
• **PM2.5** refers to fine particulate matter that can penetrate deep into the **lungs** and enter the **bloodstream**, leading to **respiratory** and **cardiovascular** diseases.
 
• The **WHO** updated its guidelines in **September 2021**, stating that annual average concentrations of **PM2.5** should not exceed **5 µg/m³**.
 
 
 
• **Most Polluted Global Rankings:**
 
 
• In recent reports, countries like **Bangladesh**, **Pakistan**, and **Tajikistan** have frequently occupied the top three spots alongside **India**.
 
• In the **2024** data, **Bangladesh** and **Pakistan** continued to report **PM2.5** levels more than **10 to 15 times** the **WHO** guideline.
 
 
 
• **Indian City Rankings:**
 
 
• Cities like **Begusarai**, **New Delhi**, and **Mullanpur** often feature in the list of the world's most polluted metropolitan areas.
 
• **New Delhi** has repeatedly been categorized as the most polluted **capital city** in the world in various editions of the **IQAir** report.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• The **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** was launched by the **Government of India** in **January 2019** to tackle air pollution in **131 cities**.
 
• The program aims for a **20% to 30%** reduction in **PM2.5** and **PM10** concentrations by **2024** (later revised to a **40%** reduction target by **2026**) compared to **2017** levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Primary Sources:** The main contributors to air pollution in **India** include **biomass burning**, **vehicle emissions**, **coal-fired power plants**, and **stubble burning** during the winter months in **Punjab** and **Haryana**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** According to various studies, air pollution costs **India** billions of dollars annually due to **healthcare expenses** and lost **labor productivity**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **World Air Quality Report** utilizes data from over **30,000** air quality monitoring stations across more than **7,000** locations in **130+ countries**.

67

questions.question: Who among the following became the youngest Formula 1 driver to win three races in a row in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kimi Antonelli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kimi Antonelli**, whose full name is **Andrea Kimi Antonelli**, made history in the **2025 Formula 1 season** by becoming the youngest driver to win three consecutive races.
 
• He achieved this milestone while driving for the **Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team**, having been promoted to the seat following the departure of **Lewis Hamilton** to **Ferrari**.
 
• Born on **August 25, 2006**, in **Bologna**, **Italy**, Antonelli was approximately **18 years** old when he secured this record-breaking hat-trick of victories. ***Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.***
 
• His streak of wins demonstrated exceptional skill and maturity, solidifying his reputation as one of the most significant talents to enter **Formula 1** in the modern era.
 
• Prior to this, the record for the youngest driver to win multiple races was held by **Max Verstappen**, but Antonelli's three-in-a-row achievement at such a young age set a new benchmark in the **FIA Formula One World Championship**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Max Verstappen**:
 
 
• He holds the record for being the youngest driver to compete in **Formula 1**, making his debut at the **2015 Australian Grand Prix** at the age of **17 years and 166 days**.
 
• **Verstappen** also became the youngest ever race winner at the **2016 Spanish Grand Prix** while driving for **Red Bull Racing**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **George Russell**:
 
 
• He is a **British** racing driver who joined **Mercedes** in **2022**.
 
• While a highly successful driver and a **Grand Prix** winner, he did not achieve a three-race winning streak as the youngest driver in **2025**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Lando Norris**:
 
 
• Driving for **McLaren**, **Norris** has established himself as a top-tier driver with multiple podiums and wins.
 
• Although he is a key contender in the championship, the specific record of being the youngest to win three consecutive races in **2025** belongs to Antonelli. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Mercedes Junior Team**:
 
 
• **Kimi Antonelli** has been a member of the **Mercedes Junior Team** since **2019**, following a dominant career in **karting** and **junior formula** categories like **Formula 4** and **Formula Regional**.
 
• His rapid ascent directly from **Formula 2** to a top-tier **Formula 1** seat is a testament to the program's success under the leadership of **Toto Wolff**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **FIA Super Licence Rules**:
 
 
• To compete in **Formula 1**, a driver must typically be **18 years** of age and have accumulated **40 points** over three seasons in eligible championships.
 
• The **FIA** introduced a relaxation in **2024** that allowed drivers aged **17** to receive a **Super Licence** under special dispensation if they demonstrated "outstanding ability," though **Antonelli** officially debuted after his **18th birthday**.
 
 
 
• **Records in Formula 1**:
 
 
• Winning three races in a row is often referred to as a "hat-trick" of wins. This feat requires immense consistency from both the driver and the **car's reliability**.
 
• The **2025 season** featured significant technological competition, making **Antonelli's** performance in the **W16** (the 2025 Mercedes car) a historic event for **Italian** motorsport.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a major application of 3D bioprinting demonstrated at MSU Vadodara in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regenerative medicine and tissue engineering**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, **Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) Vadodara** showcased major advancements in **3D bioprinting**, specifically focusing on its transformative role in **regenerative medicine and tissue engineering**.
 
• The demonstration highlighted the ability to create **complex biological structures** by utilizing **living cells** and specialized **bio-inks**, which are deposited **layer-by-layer** to form functional tissues.
 
• This technology at **MSU Vadodara** aims to address critical healthcare challenges by developing **lab-grown tissues** such as **skin grafts**, **bone scaffolds**, and **vascular networks**.
 
• The application in **regenerative medicine** focuses on the **repair** and **replacement** of damaged organs or tissues, potentially eliminating the need for traditional **organ donors** in the future.
 
• The **2025** demonstration emphasized **precision medicine**, where **3D bioprinting** is used to create patient-specific models for **surgical planning** and **drug efficacy testing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **3D Bioprinting**: This is an **additive manufacturing** process that uses **biological materials** to fabricate structures that imitate the characteristics of **natural tissues**. It differs from standard 3D printing by using **living cells** instead of plastic or metal.
 
• **Bio-inks**: These are the "inks" used in bioprinters, typically composed of **hydrogels**, **growth factors**, and **nutrients** that sustain **cell viability** and promote **proliferation** during and after the printing process.
 
• **Tissue Engineering**: This is a scientific field that combines **engineering** and **life sciences** to develop **biological substitutes**. It often uses a **scaffold** to provide a **three-dimensional** framework for cells to attach and grow.
 
• **Regenerative Medicine**: This branch of medicine seeks to **regenerate** human cells, tissues, or organs to restore **normal function**. It includes **stem cell therapy** and **bio-fabrication** as core components.
 
• **Future Applications**: Beyond tissue repair, **3D bioprinting** is expected to revolutionize **pharmaceutical research** by allowing scientists to test new **drugs** on **printed human tissues**, significantly reducing the necessity for **animal testing** and improving the accuracy of **clinical trials**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Precision and Customization**: One of the primary advantages of **3D bioprinting** is its ability to produce **anatomically accurate** structures tailored to a specific **patient's anatomy** using **MRI** or **CT scan** data.
 
• **Biocompatibility**: The materials used at institutions like **MSU Vadodara** are selected for their **biocompatibility**, ensuring that the printed tissues do not trigger an **immune rejection** when integrated with natural biological systems.
 
• **Economic Impact**: By localizing the production of **bio-printed tissues** and **scaffolds** in **India**, the technology helps in making **advanced healthcare** more **affordable** and accessible.
</ul

questions.question: As announced in 2025, the headquarters of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) will be established in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, approved the establishment of the **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)** with its permanent headquarters located in **India**.
 
• The **IBCA** was formally launched by the **Prime Minister** on **April 9, 2023**, during the **50th-anniversary** celebrations of **Project Tiger** held in **Mysuru**, **Karnataka**.
 
• The **Government of India** has committed a one-time budgetary support of **Rs. 150 crore** for a period of **five years**, spanning from **2023-24** to **2027-28**.
 
• The primary objective of the alliance is to ensure the long-term conservation of **seven major big cat species** across the globe by creating a common platform for **96 big cat range countries**.
 
• This initiative positions **India** as a global leader in wildlife conservation, as it is the only country in the world to have the **Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, and **Cheetah** (reintroduced) in its natural habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Seven Big Cats:**
 
 
• The alliance focuses on the conservation of the **Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, **Puma**, **Jaguar**, and **Cheetah**.
 
• Out of these seven species, **five** are currently found in **India**, making the country a critical stakeholder in global feline conservation.
 
 
 
• **Governance Structure:**
 
 
• The **IBCA** follows a governance model that includes a **General Assembly**, a **Council**, and a **Secretariat** (which is headquartered in **India**).
 
• The **Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change** of India plays a pivotal role in the initial administrative setup of the alliance.
 
 
 
• **Membership and Participation:**
 
 
• Membership is open to **96 range countries** that host these big cats, as well as non-range countries, **international organizations**, and scientific bodies interested in conservation.
 
• It aims to facilitate **knowledge sharing**, **capacity building**, and **resource mobilization** to mitigate human-wildlife conflict and illegal wildlife trade.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Strategies:**
 
 
• The alliance works on **benchmarking** conservation practices, **eco-tourism** development, and financial support for habitat restoration.
 
• It integrates **scientific research** with **traditional knowledge** to ensure sustainable populations of big cats in their respective **ecosystems**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Significance:** The establishment of **IBCA** is compared to the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**, showcasing **India's** intent to lead multilateral environmental frameworks.
 
• **Project Tiger Legacy:** The launch coincided with **50 years** of the **Project Tiger** initiative (started in **1973**), which has been hailed as one of the most successful species conservation programs in the world.
 
• **Financial Framework:** After the initial **five-year** grant from **India**, the **IBCA** intends to sustain itself through **membership fees**, contributions from **multilateral institutions**, and **private sector** support.
 
• **Geographical Focus:** While **India** is the headquarters, the alliance focuses heavily on regions like **Africa**, **South America**, and **Central Asia** where species like the **Jaguar** and **Snow Leopard** face significant threats.
</ul

• **Rio de Janeiro**, one of the most prominent cities in **Brazil**, has been designated as the host city for this major international event in **July 2025**.
 
• The **BRICS** chairmanship follows a rotational system among the founding and primary members: **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.
 
• Initially, **Brazil** was expected to host the **16th Summit** in **2024**, but due to logistical considerations and its **G20** presidency, the order was swapped with **Russia**, which hosted the **16th Summit** in **Kazan** in **October 2024**.

• **Evolution of BRICS:**
 
 
• The group was originally conceived as **BRIC** (**Brazil, Russia, India, and China**) in **2006**.
 
• The first formal summit took place in **Yekaterinburg, Russia**, in **2009**.
 
• With the induction of **South Africa** in **2010**, the group was renamed **BRICS**.
 
 
 
• **2024 Expansion (BRICS+):**
 
 
• Effective **January 1, 2024**, the bloc expanded to include **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE)**.
 
• This expansion reflects the group's goal of fostering a **multipolar world order** and increasing the influence of **Global South** economies.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The **BRICS** nations combined represent approximately **45% of the world's population**.
 
• The group accounts for nearly **28% of the global economy** and a significant portion of the world's oil production and trade.
 
 
 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):**
 
 
• Established during the **6th BRICS Summit** in **Fortaleza, Brazil (2014)**, the **NDB** serves as an alternative to the **World Bank** and **IMF** for infrastructure and sustainable development projects.
 
• It is headquartered in **Shanghai, China**.

• **Host City Profile:** **Rio de Janeiro** is a coastal city in **Brazil** known for its **Copacabana** and **Ipanema** beaches, and it has a long history of hosting major global events, including the **2016 Summer Olympics** and the **2024 G20 Summit**.
 
• **Summit Objectives:** The **17th Summit** is expected to focus on **strengthening multilateralism**, **sustainable energy transitions**, and **reforming international financial institutions** to better represent emerging markets.
 
• **Member Roles:** **Brazil's** leadership in **2025** is seen as a pivotal moment for the country to reassert its influence in **global diplomacy** and economic cooperation within the **Atlantic** and **South American** regions.
</ul

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India revised Priority Sector Lending (PSL) guidelines for Small Finance Banks from FY 2025–26, reducing the PSL target to what percentage of ANBC (adjusted net bank credit) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposures (CEOBE)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in a notification issued in **April 2024**, announced a significant revision to the **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** targets for **Small Finance Banks (SFBs)** to bring them on par with universal banks.
 
• As per the revised guidelines, the overall **PSL target** for **Small Finance Banks**, which was previously mandated at **75%**, will be reduced in a phased manner. For the financial year **2025–26** (specifically by **March 31, 2026**), the target has been set at **60%** of **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** or **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)**, whichever is higher.
 
• The primary objective of this revision is to provide a **level playing field** for **SFBs** and to harmonize their regulatory requirements with those of **Universal Banks**, which currently have a **40%** PSL target.
 
• Before this revision, **Small Finance Banks** were required to maintain a much higher threshold of **75%** to ensure that credit reached the **unserved and underserved sections** of the population, including small farmers and micro-units.
 
• The **RBI** has implemented a **glide path** for this transition: the target remains **75%** until **March 31, 2025**; it reduces to **60%** by **March 31, 2026**; and finally reaches **40%** by **March 31, 2027**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):** It is a **regulatory framework** established by the **RBI** that mandates banks to allocate a specific portion of their **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** to certain sectors that are considered vital for the **inclusive development** of the country. These sectors include **Agriculture**, **Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**, **Export Credit**, **Education**, **Housing**, **Social Infrastructure**, and **Renewable Energy**.
 
• **Small Finance Banks (SFBs):** These are a specific category of banks established to provide **financial inclusion** to sections of the economy not being served by other banks. They are registered as **public limited companies** under the **Companies Act, 2013** and are governed by the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**. Notable examples include **AU Small Finance Bank**, **Equitas Small Finance Bank**, and **Jana Small Finance Bank**.
 
• **ANBC and CEOBE:** **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** represents the total credit provided by a bank after making specific adjustments for bills rediscounted and other prescribed exemptions. **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)** refers to the potential credit risk from non-fund-based limits like **letters of credit** or **bank guarantees**.
 
• **Regulatory Scope:** While the overall target is being reduced, **SFBs** are still required to focus on their core mission of serving **Small and Marginal Farmers** and **Weaker Sections**. The **RBI** maintains specific sub-targets within the PSL framework to ensure these vulnerable groups continue to receive adequate credit flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for SFBs:** To be eligible for a license, the **minimum paid-up voting equity capital** for **SFBs** was initially **Rs. 100 crore**, which has been increased to **Rs. 200 crore** in recent guidelines, except for those transitioned from **Urban Co-operative Banks**.
 
• **The Glide Path Schedule:**
 
 
• **75%**: Applicable up to the end of **FY 2024-25**.
 
• **60%**: Target for the end of **FY 2025-26**.
 
• **40%**: Final target to be achieved by the end of **FY 2026-27**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Revision:** This move is expected to improve the **profitability** and **operational flexibility** of **Small Finance Banks**, as they can now diversify their loan portfolios toward higher-yielding non-priority sectors as they grow in size and scale.
 
• **Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks (UCBs):** It is important to note that **UCBs** are also on a similar glide path to reach a **75%** PSL target by **March 31, 2026**, showing the **RBI's** efforts to balance different banking tiers according to their specific mandates and risks.
